column15: It is 4:00 PM and you get 3 priority tasks: investigate a sudden spike in app uninstalls, draft a PRD for a new trivia feature, and define mutually exclusive user segments for an upcoming funnel analysis report. You only have time to properly complete one before logging off. How do you handle this?
column16: A vocal group of users on social media is demanding a "live fan chat" feature during matches. It sounds exciting, but it has not been built. How do you figure out whether this is actually a good idea for the app, or a noisy distraction?
column17: You need to summarise 500 open-text user reviews from the app store and present the top three actionable feature requests to the team in one hour. How do you do it?
column18: You have a major feature idea, but there is zero engineering bandwidth for the next two weeks. What exactly do you do during this time?
column19: You strongly believe a new engagement feature must go live before a major tournament, but a senior stakeholder completely disagrees on its priority. How do you proceed?
column20: A new leaderboard drives engagement, but within 3 days the top 10 positions are clearly held by bots or spam accounts farming points. Engineering bandwidth is zero. How do you handle this right now to protect the real user experience?
column21: A major competitor just launched a heavily marketed AI stats feature. Leadership asks whether you should build a clone immediately so you do not fall behind. How do you evaluate whether this is actually the right move?

column15: First the uninstall spike: it is live user harm, so I check the release log, crash rate in Firebase and uninstall cohorts by app version and OS within 30 minutes, and loop in the on-call engineer. Second the segments, because analysts are blocked on them; I define mutually exclusive groups by activity tier in a shared doc. The trivia PRD is important but not urgent, so I draft the problem statement tonight and finish it tomorrow morning, and I tell my manager this order and why.
column16: I would size the demand before building: count unique posters versus total MAU, run a 5-question in-app survey to a random 5% sample, and check how many users already use WhatsApp groups during matches. Then a fake-door test: a "Join match chat" button for 10% of users and measure click-through. If CTR is above 8% and the survey shows retention intent, we pilot a moderated chat for one marquee match and track session length and D7 retention against a holdout.
column17: I would export the 500 reviews to a sheet, use an LLM to tag each with a theme and sentiment, then manually check 50 tags for accuracy. Group by theme, count frequency, and weight by rating and recency. Pick the top three requests that are frequent, recent and feasible, each with two verbatim quotes and the count, on one slide.
column18: I spend the two weeks de-risking: interview 8 users, write the PRD with success metrics and edge cases, make Figma wireframes and test them with 5 users, and size impact with data. I also get engineering to review the spec for 30 minutes so estimates are ready the day bandwidth opens.
column19: I would first understand why the stakeholder disagrees, then bring data: projected engagement lift from last season tournament traffic and the cost of shipping late. I would propose a smaller MVP behind a flag to cut risk. If we still disagree, I agree on a decision owner and a deadline and escalate with both options written down, then commit to the decision.
column20: Protect real users today: hide accounts with abnormal point velocity from the public board using a simple rule in the admin panel, add a note that rankings are under review, and freeze prizes. Then sample 20 flagged accounts manually to check false positives. Next sprint, ask for rate limits and device fingerprinting.
column21: I would not clone immediately. I check whether our users actually want AI stats through search logs and a survey, look at the competitor reviews and adoption signals, and compare it with our strategy and current roadmap bets. If there is a real signal, run a small experiment with a lightweight version and measure engagement and retention before committing a full team.

If CTR is above 8% and the survey shows retention intent, we pilot a moderated chat for one marquee match and track session length and D7 retention against a holdout. I would propose a smaller MVP behind a flag to cut risk. If we still disagree, I agree on a decision owner and a deadline and escalate with both options written down, then commit to the decision.
column20: Protect real users today: hide accounts with abnormal point velocity from the public board using a simple rule in the admin panel, add a note that rankings are under review, and freeze prizes. Then sample 20 flagged accounts manually to check false positives. Next sprint, ask for rate limits and device fingerprinting.
column21: I would not clone immediately. I check whether our users actually want AI stats through search logs and a survey, look at the competitor reviews and adoption signals, and compare it with our strategy and current roadmap bets. If there is a real signal, run a small experiment with a lightweight version and measure engagement and retention before committing a full team.
